_note: Values copied from the quoted passages of the papers named in each entry.

brs22._source: Bos, Renes, Sprenkels, ePrint 2022/323 (AFRICACRYPT 2022), Table 2 'This work', rows S (Sign): 'S 5.0 18 470 6.5 36 303 8.1 44 332' (KiB, kcc), 'All cycle counts were averaged over 10 000 iterations'; platform STM32F407 (Cortex-M4) at 24 MHz; round-3 Dilithium.

aln25._source: Alnahawi et al., ePrint 2025/812 section 3.1: 'The chip had approximately 4.5kB of RAM available for our cryptographic operations, and around 3kB of this was used during execution.' Part: 'NXP SmartMX3 P71D600'; 'Java Card implementation of ML-KEM'; 'ISO/IEC 7816 contact interface'.

kl29._source: EMV SWG NP62r2, Notice Bulletin No. 29, July 2025 (inputs): '1984-bit keys are recommended to have an anticipated lifetime to at least 31 December 2035.'; '256-bit and 521-bit ECC keys are recommended to have an anticipated lifetime beyond 31 December 2035.'; '1408-bit keys are recommended to have expired 31 December 2024.'

pqeac._source: Fischlin et al., ePrint 2023/352, implementation section: 'The security controller comes with significantly increased RAM-size of 96 kBytes'. Benchmarking: 'For PQ-EAC, we reliably measured a total runtime of 1.28 seconds.'

nxp_blog._source: NXP blog, J. Renes, 10 Nov 2025, read directly in a browser on 2026-09-30 (page text SHA-256 4836990e9a39ec724a8e6641b55d2ecf1e0ad27d4e048fee01169f6d90a5b390).
nxp_blog.quote: Next-generation secure elements, serving the mobile, Industrial IoT and secure identity markets, will also feature dedicated PQC hardware support and can be included as a ready-to-use solution for any Integrated Circuit (IC).

bdg25._source: Bettale, Dottax, Gremy, SECRYPT 2025 p.117: 'a typical embedded device (32-bit Cortex-M3 CPU at 100 MHz) with a hardware accelerator for ECC. The chip supports a baud-rate of 600 kbit/s.'; 'The ML-KEM primitives were implemented with side-channel countermeasures'. Table 3 (p.118, ML-DSA) and Table 4 (FN-DSA), Mode B 128: processing 290 ms (ratio x6.0). ePrint 2024/2005 Table 4 (classic ECC SCP11), Mode B 128: processing 48 ms. Mode B (Fig. 6, PQ part): card runs KEM.KeyGen (ephemeral), KEM.Decaps(KEM.skC, c.Ss), KEM.Decaps(KEM.eskC, c.Se); no signature verification by the card.

dz26._source: Dottax, Zeitoun, ePrint 2026/1274 sec. 4: 'a production-grade smart card platform embedding a secure element designed for banking and identity applications, and running at 50 MHz'; Table 2: ML-KEM-512 + CMAC-AES-128 '3.58 + 0.46 = 4.04' (normalised to ECDSA-256); ML-DSA-44 '20.5 - 307.7'; communication at 848 kbit/s.
